claim: Interface design alone, with the model fixed, changes agent success a lot: a purpose-built agent-computer interface beat a plain shell by 7 points absolute (11.00 to 18.00 on SWE-bench Lite, GPT-4 Turbo; 64% relative). The paper text says 10.7 points, which does not match its own table. Gap search: On 2025 models a bash-only shell already resolves 60-74% on SWE-bench Verified (Live-SWE-agent Table 1) and a designed layer adds about 3-5 points (63.0 vs 59.8 GPT-5-Mini; 75.4 vs 70.6 Claude 4.5 Sonnet); the 7-point 2024 gain was against a weak shell baseline. Token-equal tests are still missing.
agent_test: Same model, same tokens: raw tool/shell access vs a designed command set; score at equal token budget.

claim: Guardrail feedback at the point of error (lint-blocked edits) helps: edit with linting 18.0 vs without 15.0 vs no edit tool 10.3 (Lite). One run on 300 tasks, so the 3-point part is near noise.
agent_test: Add or remove a code-side validator on the model output at equal tokens; measure pass rate.

claim: More interface is not always better: iterative search (12.0) was worse than no search (15.7); summarised search 18.0; 100-line window 18.0 beats 30 lines (14.3) and full file (12.7). Human UIs make poor model interfaces.
agent_test: Vary how much of the working state the code shows per step (summary vs full vs paged).

claim: Interleaving thought with tool action beats acting without thought (ALFWorld ReAct 71 vs Act 45), but on knowledge QA the mix is not uniformly best (HotpotQA ReAct 27.4 vs CoT 29.4; best was ReAct to CoT-SC 35.1).
agent_test: Compare think+tool vs tool-only vs think-only at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Offloading arithmetic or execution to an interpreter beats model-only reasoning, most when numbers are large (PAL GSM8K 72.0 vs CoT about 57; GSM-HARD 61.2 vs CoT 23.3).
agent_test: Route exact computation to code; compare vs CoT on large-number items.

claim: An external written workspace (scratchpad) lifts multi-step computation (polynomial eval few-shot 8.8 to 20.1; program execution 11 to 26.5).
agent_test: Scratchpad vs direct answer at equal output tokens.

claim: Code as the action format beats JSON/text actions (up to 20 points higher success, up to 30% fewer actions, 17 LLMs).
agent_test: Code-action vs JSON-action for the same tools.

claim: Forcing strict structured output (JSON/XML) can cut reasoning accuracy (GSM8K gpt-4o-mini 94.57 NL vs 86.95 JSON-mode); parsing errors do not explain it; JSON-schema and classification can be neutral or help. Gap search: Strong 2025-26 closed models show near-zero format tax (Format Tax; Sonnet 4.6 88.7 JSON vs 89.3 CoT), but the tax returns near the capability limit (Haiku 4.5 -36.2 points; Opus 4.7 AIME 96.2 to 91.0), and a reasoning-first field or two-step reformat recovers most of it. JSONSchemaBench shows no harm when a reasoning field comes first.
agent_test: Free reasoning first, then format in a second step; compare to inline structured output.

claim: Meaning-neutral format changes shift accuracy by large amounts (up to 76 points LLaMA-2-13B; about 10 on average; GPT-3.5 up to 56). Best format differs by model and task.
agent_test: Test two or three layouts of the same state on our model; fix the winner.

claim: Position in context matters: accuracy falls when the key fact is mid-context, below closed-book (56.1) with 20 documents for GPT-3.5. Only 2023 models tested; no evidence yet for current models. Gap search: Length alone costs accuracy even with perfect retrieval (13.9% to 85% drops, Du et al. 2025) and 11 of 13 models fall under 50% of baseline at 32K (NoLiMa). Position of checks and goals in code-laid-out state is still untested.
agent_test: Put key facts and open checks at start and end vs middle on the current model.

claim: Short tool documentation beats demonstrations for unfamiliar tools (F1 0.37-0.45 docs only vs 0.05-0.19 best few-shot; docs plus demos no better).
agent_test: Write one-paragraph manuals per code tool; ablate manual vs examples.

claim: Too many tools in the prompt hurt selection; retrieving relevant tools first raised accuracy (43.13 vs 13.62 all-tools) and cut prompt tokens by about half. A poor retriever hurt badly in Gorilla (-21.5 and -47.6). Gap search: Per-state retrieval cut tool loading by up to 50% with unchanged accuracy (Dynamic ReAct); parameter schema design shifts tool choice (Li et al. 2026). No equal-prompt-size comparison with a fixed small set.
agent_test: Show only the tools needed for the current state.

claim: Paged external memory with model-driven retrieval lifts recall of old context (MemGPT deep memory retrieval 32.1 to 92.5 for GPT-4).
agent_test: Compare full-history vs retrieved memory at equal tokens.

claim: Stored verbal reflection after failed trials helps the next trial (HumanEval pass@1 91 vs 80), yet SWE-agent found full history (15.0) worse than last-5 observations (18.0). Memory content and amount interact.
agent_test: Test stored reflections vs recent-only context.

claim: Cognitive operations as callable tools raise math scores (GPT-4.1 AIME2024 32.0 to 53.0; cognitive prompting 42.0).
agent_test: Run operators as separate code-called calls vs one prompt, at equal tokens.

claim: A fixed pipeline without an agent loop can match interface-heavy agents at lower cost (Agentless GPT-4 32.00% Lite, $0.70 per issue), so the interface gain depends on the baseline and the benchmark era.
agent_test: Scripted pipeline vs free agent loop at equal cost.

claim: Tool-using agents are unreliable across repeats: tau-bench gpt-4o pass^1 61% retail, 35% airline, pass^8 under 25% in retail.
agent_test: Report pass^k, not only pass@1.

claim: Humans offload too eagerly when metacognition is poor; prediction plus feedback improves calibrated offloading (Ngai and Gilbert 2026: underconfidence -14.5 to -6.3; N=164, replicated N=416).
agent_test: Make the model predict its own success before choosing tool vs recall; score the choice.

claim: Trusted reliable reminders shift effort away from self-maintenance of intentions (Dupre and Ball 2026, N=320). Automation-complacency literature is consistent but was not opened.
agent_test: Check whether the model stops checking when the code is always right.

claim: The Google Stroop effect (Sparrow 2011) did not replicate: Hesselmann N=89, BF01 5.07 for the null; the Camerer project replication also failed.
agent_test: Not needed; drop the claim that web access primes retrieval words.

claim: The phone-presence brain-drain effect did not replicate in a pre-registered study, though a meta-analysis (22 studies, 43 effects) found a negative overall effect with high heterogeneity.
agent_test: Low priority; mere presence of unused tools is not a cost for the model.

claim: Handwriting vs laptop notes: laptop notes more verbatim but no quiz penalty in a direct replication (n=74 vs 68).
agent_test: Do not assume artifact format alone changes encoding.

claim: Heavy use of an aid is linked to weaker unaided skill or ownership: GPS (50 drivers; 13 retested), LLM essays (Kosmyna: 15/18 LLM users failed to quote in session 1 vs 2/18; session 4 7/9 vs 1/9). Gap search: For frozen models there is no carry-over; fine-tuned models show scaffold-convention dependence (DCAS: 49.7% to 20.4% off-scaffold) while untrained base models do not.
agent_test: Small N, correlational or preprint. Test: remove the aid mid-run and watch recovery.

claim: Searching the web inflates people's sense of their own knowledge (9 experiments).
agent_test: Check if tool access raises model stated confidence without raising accuracy.

claim: Epistemic actions: acting physically cuts mental cost (Tetris rotation 100 ms vs 800-1200 ms mental; false starts cost 75-750 ms), supporting cheap probes before full planning. Gap search: Kirsh and Maglio text read: 100 ms vs 800-1200 ms is from a 3-player pilot and is an estimate.
agent_test: Allow cheap probe steps before commit; count tokens saved.

claim: Moving rules from memory into the display lowers error in Tower of Hanoi isomorphs (all errors on internal rules; N 18, 24, 36).
agent_test: Show active constraints in each prompt vs only in the system prompt.

claim: Models over-trust corrupted tool returns: mean adoption of a plausible wrong return was 68.0% (search), 40.1% (sub-agent), 35.5% (code executor) across 14 models; corrupted returns overrode previously correct answers in 26.8-56.4% of items; users were warned in 4.2% of final answers. A verification instruction reduced adoption on all three tools; reliability labels only partly.
agent_test: Inject a wrong tool return at a known rate; compare adoption with and without a verification instruction and a code-side cross-check, at equal tokens.

claim: Models call tools they do not need: Llama tool overuse above 50% in a preliminary study; training for self-awareness cut tool calls 24% and raised performance over 37%. Whether prompting plus feedback does this on current models is not tested.
agent_test: Prompt the model to predict whether it can answer without a tool, give feedback on its predictions, and measure call rate and accuracy.

claim: Repeating earlier content each turn only partly fixes multi-turn loss: 15-20% recovery with GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini; average multi-turn drop 39%; reasoning models degrade the same. Practitioner reports say just-in-time user-role reminders raise rule compliance, but no controlled numbers exist.
schema_part: G guardrails in each S prompt
agent_test: A/B test: rules only in the system prompt vs rules re-stated in each state prompt, counting constraint violations at equal tokens.

claim: Acting to gain information beat thinking more at equal compute in a web agent (WebArena 23% to 28% with check-again prompting vs under 3% for budget forcing or best-of-n), but too many re-checks hurt. No test of cheap probes in code tasks.
agent_test: Compare a one-step probe (run a test, inspect a value) before each commit against no probe, with tokens counted.

claim: A bare scaffold can carry the result: a rule-based script with no LLM scored 96.8 against about 97.5 for top LLM configurations in one agent benchmark. A benchmark must include a scaffold-only control.
agent_test: Run a no-model or random-model arm through the scaffold on each benchmark item.

claim: Tool and memory disagree often: conflict rate 14.1% (GPT-4o) to 83.2% (Llama-3 8B), mean 49.8%; math accuracy falls 4.5 points under conflict; prompting and RAG fixes did not resolve it.
agent_test: Add a reconcile step that runs a second independent check when model and tool disagree.

claim: Founding human numbers: Kirsh and Maglio pilot (3 Tetris players) supports 100 ms physical vs 800-1200 ms mental rotation. Larkin and Simon 1987, Norman 1991 and Hutchins 1995 remain unread in full.
agent_test: none
